title: Conveyor drive ignores the PLC
summary: After a drive inspection the conveyor no longer starts. The PLC sends the run command, the drive shows no fault, and the motor does not turn.
objectives: Check whether a command really reaches a device and whether the device accepts it
Use drive status feedback as evidence
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open: TRUE while pressed. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while NOT pressed (wire-break safe). *)
    DriveReady : BOOL; (* Drive relay output 'ready': TRUE while the drive is powered and not tripped. *)
    DriveRunning : BOOL; (* Drive relay output 'running': TRUE while the drive is turning the motor. *)
    DriveRemote : BOOL; (* Drive relay output 'remote': TRUE while the drive accepts its run terminal (remote/terminal control). *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    DriveRun : BOOL; (* Drive run terminal: TRUE requests the drive to run. *)
    RunLamp : BOOL; (* Green run lamp H1. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Request : BOOL;
END_VAR

Request := (StartPB OR Request) AND StopPB AND DriveReady;
DriveRun := Request;
RunLamp := DriveRunning;

END_PROGRAM
instructions: Run the simulation and press Start; confirm the symptom.
Compare the PLC run command with what the drive reports on its display.
Check the drive's feedback signals DriveReady, DriveRunning and DriveRemote.
hints: The PLC can only request the drive to run; the drive decides whether it accepts the request.
Which drive signal tells you whether the drive listens to its terminals?

troubleshooting.symptom: Since the drive was inspected this morning, pressing Start does nothing: the conveyor stays still and the run lamp stays dark. No drive fault is shown and the PLC shows DriveRun TRUE.

diagnosisOptions.label: The PLC program does not set the run command
The digital output module has no load supply
The drive is in Local (keypad) control and ignores its run terminal
The drive has tripped on a fault

repairs.label: Switch the drive's control source back to Remote (terminal control)

debrief.rootCause: The conveyor drive was left in Local (keypad) control after maintenance. In Local the drive ignores its run terminal, so the PLC's run command arrived but was not accepted.
evidence: DriveRun was TRUE in the PLC and the drive's display showed the run terminal ON: the command reached the drive.
DriveReady stayed TRUE, so the drive was powered and not tripped.
DriveRemote was FALSE and the drive's display showed LOC instead of REM.
DriveRunning stayed FALSE and the motor speed stayed at 0 Hz although the command was present.
debrief.repair: Switch the drive's control source back to Remote (terminal control), then verify that Start runs the conveyor and Stop stops it.
debrief.reasoning: When a command reaches a device but the device does not act, check the device's own state before the wiring or the program. Drives, valves with manual overrides and local panels all have a local/remote selection that overrides the PLC.
